questions.q: What does a Pause condition do to a running task_sla instance?
options: It ends the SLA permanently, marking it Achieved
It immediately marks the SLA as Breached
It suspends time accumulation without ending the SLA, resuming where it left off
It resets the elapsed time back to zero
questions.explain: Pause suspends the clock; it resumes exactly where it left off once the Pause condition no longer matches.

questions.q: Why is `state = On Hold AND hold_reason = Awaiting Caller` a well-scoped Pause condition?
options: It pauses the clock specifically while the team is waiting on the customer, time the team doesn't control
It pauses the SLA for every On Hold reason equally
It has no effect on `task_sla` behavior
It stops the SLA permanently instead of pausing it
questions.explain: Scoping Pause to the specific Awaiting Caller reason prevents customer wait time from counting against the team's target, without masking other hold time.

questions.q: What happens if an SLA's duration elapses before its Stop condition is met?
options: The instance is marked Achieved by default
The instance is marked Breached
Nothing — the SLA simply closes quietly with no outcome recorded
The instance automatically resets and restarts
questions.explain: If duration reaches 100% before Stop fires, the task_sla instance is marked Breached.

questions.q: What does attaching an '8-5 Weekdays' `cmn_schedule` to an SLA Definition change?
options: Nothing — schedules only affect reporting, not SLA duration math
It makes the SLA duration count only during defined business hours instead of running 24/7
It forces every SLA to use a 24/7 countdown regardless of the schedule
It changes the Applies To condition instead of the duration calculation
questions.explain: A real schedule record makes SLA duration business-hour-aware — a 4-hour target pauses outside the defined hours rather than counting wall-clock time.

questions.q: Why is a Stop condition that never matches a record's real resolution path a serious implementation bug?
options: It automatically fixes itself the next time the record is updated
The clock keeps running on a record long after it was actually resolved, distorting breach data
It only affects Priority 3 and lower incidents
It has no real effect on the SLA's outcome
questions.explain: If Stop never fires, the task_sla clock keeps counting against a record that's already been resolved, inflating or masking breach counts.
